title: Industrial Paper Factory: From Pulp to Finished Roll
topic: Manufacturing Engineering & Pulp and Paper Technology
pedagogical_goal: This simulation demonstrates the core unit operations of a modern paper factory: pulping, refining, sheet formation on a Fourdrinier wire, pressing, drying, and calendering. Users will understand how raw wood or recycled fiber is transformed into a continuous paper web, and how key process variables (refining energy, moisture content, drying temperature) affect final paper properties such as thickness, density, and tensile strength.

fundamental_laws: Mass conservation: Input dry fiber mass = Output dry fiber mass + losses
Water removal kinetics: Rate of evaporation ∝ (T_dry - T_wet) * surface_area * air_flow
Fiber bonding theory: Tensile strength ∝ (refining_energy)^0.5 * (1 - moisture_content)^2
Newtonian fluid flow for stock: Flow rate ∝ pressure_drop / viscosity
Heat transfer in drying cylinders: Q = h * A * (T_cylinder - T_web)

components.description: Layer 1: Factory floor with safety yellow grid lines, structural columns, and overhead crane rails. Includes faint ISO safety symbols and process flow diagram in background.

Layer 2: Massive paper machine silhouette comprising headbox, Fourdrinier wire section, press section, dryer section (6 cylinders), and calender stack. Occupies ~75% of canvas height, built from closed Bezier paths with shading.

Layer 3: Moving paper web visualized as a semi-transparent sheet with dynamic opacity and color gradient representing moisture content. Shows stock jet impingement on wire and water removal progression.

Layer 4: 30 animated elements including: 10 fiber particles showing flocculation/dispersion, 5 water droplets being removed, 5 rotating dryer cylinder shells, 5 press roll nips, and 5 calender roll surfaces. All driven by GSAP timelines.

animation_mapping.fiber_particle: translation along web path with Brownian motion
animation_mapping.water_droplet: radial ejection from web surface during pressing
animation_mapping.calender_surface: rotation with web, speed proportional to fourdrinier_speed

components.description: Layer 5: In-situ process control badges: (1) Refining energy monitor on refiner vessel, (2) Moisture sensor array after press section, (3) Dryer surface temperature probes, (4) Basis weight gauge on reel, (5) Tensile strength tester schematic near calender.

pedagogical_callouts.title: Stock Preparation & Refining
pedagogical_callouts.text: Wood chips or recycled fiber are pulped and refined. Increasing refining energy fibrillates fibers, increasing surface area for bonding but also energy consumption. Optimal refining balances strength development with drainage resistance.

pedagogical_callouts.title: Sheet Formation on Fourdrinier Wire
pedagogical_callouts.text: Diluted stock (0.5% consistency) is jetted onto a moving wire. Water drains by gravity and vacuum, forming a fragile web. Fourdrinier speed determines production rate and influences fiber orientation and formation quality.

pedagogical_callouts.title: Pressing and Drying Sections
pedagogical_callouts.text: The wet web passes through nips of press rolls to remove water mechanically, then through steam-heated dryer cylinders where evaporation completes moisture removal. Dryer temperature and web residence time dictate final moisture content and energy efficiency.

pedagogical_callouts.title: Calendering and Reeling
pedagogical_callouts.text: The dry web passes through calender rolls to smooth surface and control thickness. Finally, it is wound onto a reel. Final paper properties depend on the entire process history, particularly refining and drying conditions.
